questions.stem: Show that $\tan^4\theta-1\equiv\dfrac{1-2\cos^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta}$.

questions.label: 2(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the curve $y=k\cos\left(x-\tfrac16\pi\right)$ where $k$ is a positive constant and $x$ is measured in radians. The curve crosses the $x$-axis at point $A$ and $B$ is a minimum point.

Find the coordinates of $A$ and $B$.

figures.alt: Axes with origin O. Cosine-type wave y = k cos(x − π/6) for x ≥ 0: starts at a positive value on the y-axis, rises to a maximum, falls through the x-axis to a minimum, rises through the x-axis at A (marked), up to a maximum, down to a second minimum B (marked), then rises again through the x-axis.

questions.label: 2(b)
questions.stem: Find the exact value of $t$ that satisfies the equation $$3\sin^{-1}(3t)+2\cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac12\sqrt2\right)=\pi.$$
Prove the identity $\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1-\sin\theta}-\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}\equiv\tan\theta$.
Show that $\dfrac{\tan\theta}{1+\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\tan\theta}{1-\cos\theta}\equiv\dfrac{2}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$.

questions.label: 5(a)
questions.stem: Prove the identity $\dfrac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{1+\cos x}\equiv-\cos x$.

questions.label: 5(b)
questions.stem: Hence solve the equation $\dfrac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{2+2\cos x}=\dfrac14$ for $0^\circ\leqslant x\leqslant360^\circ$.
Solve the equation $\dfrac{\tan\theta+3\sin\theta+2}{\tan\theta-3\sin\theta+1}=2$ for $0^\circ\leqslant\theta\leqslant90^\circ$.

questions.label: 7(a)
questions.stem: Prove the identity $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin\theta}+\dfrac{1}{1+\sin\theta}\equiv\dfrac{2}{\cos^2\theta}$.

questions.label: 7(b)
questions.stem: Hence, solve the equation $\dfrac{3}{1-\sin\theta}+\dfrac{3}{1+\sin\theta}=12$ for $0^\circ\leqslant\theta\leqslant360^\circ$.
Given that $x>0$, find the two smallest values of $x$, in radians, for which $3\tan(2x+1)=1$. Show all necessary working.

questions.label: 9(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows a right-angled triangle $PQR$. The point $S$ lies on $PR$ and is such that $PS=4RS$. The distance $RS=a$. The angle $QPR=\tfrac16\pi$ radians, and the angle $PQS=\theta$ radians.

Find the exact distance $QS$ in terms of $a$. Give your answer in the form $\sqrt{\dfrac{c}{d}}\,a$, where $c$ and $d$ are integers to be found.

figures.alt: Right-angled triangle PQR with the right angle at R. P, S and R lie on one straight line, S between P and R. Q is the third vertex. Solid straight lines PQ, QR, PR and QS. Labels: angle QPR = 1/6 π rad at P; angle PQS = θ rad at Q; RS = a marked on PR near R.

questions.label: 9(b)(i)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows a right-angled triangle $PQR$. The point $S$ lies on $PR$ and is such that $PS=4RS$. The distance $RS=a$. The angle $QPR=\tfrac16\pi$ radians, and the angle $PQS=\theta$ radians.

Show that the angle $RQS=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{21}}{14}\right)$.

figures.alt: Right-angled triangle PQR with the right angle at R. P, S and R lie on one straight line, S between P and R. Q is the third vertex. Solid straight lines PQ, QR, PR and QS. Labels: angle QPR = 1/6 π rad at P; angle PQS = θ rad at Q; RS = a marked on PR near R.

questions.stem: Show that the equation $$6\sin\theta+\frac{1}{\tan\theta}=\frac{4}{\sin\theta}$$ can be written in the form $$6\cos^2\theta-\cos\theta-2=0.$$
Show that $\dfrac{\sin\theta+2\cos\theta}{\cos\theta-2\sin\theta}-\dfrac{\sin\theta-2\cos\theta}{\cos\theta+2\sin\theta}\equiv\dfrac4{5\cos^2\theta-4}$.

questions.label: 12(a)
questions.stem: Prove the identity $\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\equiv\dfrac{2}{\cos\theta}$.

questions.label: 12(b)
questions.stem: Hence solve the equation $\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\dfrac{3}{\sin\theta}$, for $0\leqslant\theta\leqslant2\pi$.
Show that $3\tan^2\theta+5\sin^2\theta\equiv\dfrac{8\sin^2\theta-5\sin^4\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}$.
Prove the identity $\dfrac{1-2\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}\equiv1-\tan^2\theta$.
It is given that $\beta$ is an angle between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ such that $\sin\beta=a$. Express $\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta$ in terms of $a$.

questions.label: 16(a)
questions.stem: Prove the identity $\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1-\sin x}-\dfrac{1-\sin x}{1+\sin x}\equiv\dfrac{4\tan x}{\cos x}$.

questions.label: 16(b)
questions.stem: Hence solve the equation $\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1-\sin x}-\dfrac{1-\sin x}{1+\sin x}=8\tan x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant\tfrac12\pi$.
It is given that $\alpha=\cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac8{17}\right)$. Find, without using the trigonometric functions on your calculator, the exact value of $\dfrac1{\sin\alpha}+\dfrac1{\tan\alpha}$.

questions.label: 18(a)
questions.stem:
The equation of a curve is $y=4\cos2x+3$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

State the greatest and least possible values of $y$.

questions.label: 18(b)
questions.stem:
The equation of a curve is $y=4\cos2x+3$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

Sketch the curve.

figures.alt: Blank axes for the sketch: x-axis from O marked ½π, π, 3π/2, 2π; y-axis unmarked.

questions.label: 19(a)
questions.stem:
A curve has equation $y=2+3\sin\tfrac12x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant4\pi$.

State greatest and least values of $y$.

questions.label: 19(b)
questions.stem:
A curve has equation $y=2+3\sin\tfrac12x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant4\pi$.

Sketch the curve.
Prove the identity $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}\equiv\dfrac{\tan^2\theta+1}{\tan^2\theta-1}$.

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=k\sin\tfrac12x$, where $k$ is a positive constant and $x$ is measured in radians. The curve has a minimum point $A$.

State the coordinates of $A$.

figures.alt: Curve y = k sin(x/2) from O (x = 0) to x = 6π on the x-axis: maximum at x = π, zero at x = 2π, minimum point A at x = 3π, zero at x = 4π, maximum at x = 5π, and it ends on the x-axis at x = 6π. Axes Ox (labelled x) and Oy (labelled y), origin O.

questions.stem: Show that the equation $5\cos\theta-\sin\theta\tan\theta+1=0$ may be expressed in the form $a\cos^2\theta+b\cos\theta+c=0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants to be found.
Sketch the graph of $y=3\sin x+2$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

questions.stem: Show that the equation $\dfrac1{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}+\dfrac1{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}=1$ may be expressed in the form $a\sin^2\theta+b\sin\theta+c=0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants to be found.

questions.label: 25(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=p\sin(q\theta)+r$, where $p$, $q$ and $r$ are constants.

State the value of $p$.
